newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebronites need thick skin for hard-head jokes.
newsitem.headline: Hebronites need thick skin for hard-head jokes.

text.p: There's not much to laugh about in Hebron, a powderkeg of Arab-Jewish violence. But that doesn't stop the jokes.
The city, in the news for holding up Israeli-Palestinian peace, is also famous as an inexhaustible source of one-liners.
"Have you heard about the Hebronite who...?" is a refrain in school yards and coffee shops of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Above all, a reputation for being hard-headed has made Hebronites the butt of thousands of jokes. Some are in dubious taste.
If a Hebronite falls head first off a building, the only casualty is the pavement. Same thing if he walks into a wall.
Hebronites seem remarkably good-humoured about the ridiculing. They make up some of the jokes.

"Hebronites are tremendously proud and self-confident," said Younis Amr, head of Hebron University. "They don't care about being made fun of. They know they are stronger personalities than those telling the jokes," he said, without a hint of self-mockery.
So why do other Palestinians poke fun at them? "Jealousy, admiration," says Amr, launching into a long explanation of how the city's turbulent history has moulded its 100,000 inhabitants' character.

Deep-rooted clans, a close-knit community, frugality, strong conservative and Islamic values, toughness, even the relative isolation and ruggedness of the Judean hills have formed the Hebronite mind, Amr says.
Outsiders sometimes turn these virtues on their head. Close family ties become in-breeding, caution becomes dim-wittedness, toughness is mule-like obstinacy, frugality is penny-pinching.
"Arab society tends to see things in black and white," says Abdellatif Barghouti, a Palestinian folklore expert at Bir Zeit University.

"The jokes represent them as being either too stupid or too clever. Schoolchildren tell jokes such as: 'Why do people in Hebron put their TV sets on tall stands? So they can see the announcer's legs,'" Barghouti said.
Adults add stubbornness and tight-fistedness to their jokes.
But it may be Hebron that has the last laugh. The same characteristics that have other Palestinians in stitches have Hebronites in riches.

Hebron counts more millionaires than most other Palestinian cities. Hebronites are astute businessmen, running many of the stores in East Jerusalem, Ramallah and Nablus. Hebronites also own huge companies in Jordan.
